subject: Request: Dedicated uptime & latency commitment for RiverMark

Subject: Request: Dedicated uptime & latency commitments for RiverMark

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. RiverMark is ready to move to a committed contract but they need two things signed off before procurement can issue a PO: a regional uptime commitment (we need 99.95% across our primary US region) and a latency commitment for inference (p95 <= 250ms for the model family they will serve).

Attached is their formal SLA request and some recent production latency traces. They explicitly ask that commitments apply to the dedicated deployment we discussed (reserved GPU pool) and include an operational fallback if we have cross-region disruptions.

Can you please confirm whether Redwood can support these as an exception for a marquee account? RiverMark is offering a 24-month committed spend and has legal already standing by. Procurement wants a response by EOD Tuesday to keep the renewal cadence.

Attachments: rivermark_sla_request_v2.pdf (application/pdf), latency-metrics-202703.csv (text/csv)

Thanks,
Elena Park

RiverMark Analytics

Elena — thanks for the doc and the traces. Laura / Marissa — looping you in. Karthik, can you tee up feasibility and the minimal set of engineering changes required to make this an approved carve-out? High level asks:

- 99.95% regional uptime for dedicated pool (primary US)
- p95 inference latency <= 250ms for the target model family at their expected QPS
- Regional fallback behavior (automatic cross-region failover to secondary pool)

A few quick notes on definitions we should align on: what window is the uptime measured over (monthly rolling vs quarterly), what qualifies as a downtime event (service vs infra), and whether credits / SLA penalties are fixed or tiered.

From product/infra perspective I expect this will require: dedicated capacity pinning, prioritization policy for their route, and an agreed runbook for cross-region failover. From ops/finance we may need a written credit schedule. From legal: carveouts in our standard SOW.

I'll run a short internal approval path (product -> infra -> legal -> finance). If this is materially custom we should budget an implementation & documentation charge. Laura, can you confirm the proposed committed ARR and the timeline? Elena, if you can flag any hard stop dates from RiverMark that helps prioritization.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni

Quick commercial context: RiverMark expects to commit $1.2M ARR for 24 months (reserved pool + premium support). Their procurement team flagged the EOD Tue deadline as internal. They are a strategic customer — public reference and potential referral to a marketplace partner.

They are flexible on exact wording but want formal SLAs in the MSA or an appended SOW. If product wants to propose mitigations (e.g., stricter routing, warm standby in eu-west), I can negotiate in parallel.

We need to know: estimated implementation lift, monthly cost delta for dedicated pinning and cross-region standby, and proposed SLA credit terms (for example: 5% credit per quarter below threshold capped at X%).

Happy to take point on commercial paperwork once we get technical sign-off.

—Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated uptime & latency commitments for RiverMark

Thanks — I reviewed the attachment and latency traces. Short answer: feasible with constraints. Details below: 

- Uptime: 99.95% regional is achievable if RiverMark is on a dedicated pool with a hot-standby in another AZ or region and we guarantee operator-on-call for incident remediation. That requires an infra policy change to pin their routes and reserve N% headroom in the pool (we should quantify N).

- Latency: p95 <= 250ms is doable for small/medium models on A100/4x setups at modest QPS, but for larger models their traces suggest spikes; to meet p95 we likely need: inference CPUs tuned, model quantization guidance or smaller model family, and strict scheduling (no noisy neighbors) — effectively dedicated vCPU/GPU allocations. If they require guaranteed p95 at specified concurrency (they should provide target QPS) we'll need to test with their prompt set.

- Fallback: cross-region failover is possible but will increase tail latency during failover and could violate p95 during the switch window; we can offer an SLA that provides a best-effort failover with a credit schedule for extended failover times.

Action items for product/engineering to estimate: 
1) Define exact measurement windows & SLI definitions (monthly rolling window; p95 measured at the inference latency point with our edge proxy included).
2) Quantify capacity reservation headroom and incremental monthly cost.
3) Run a focused load test with RiverMark prompt set and provide a runbook for failover.

I'll take #1 and #2. Marissa — can you help scope load test infra and tagging? Vivek/Laura — please confirm target QPS and model family.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP Product | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Internal: RiverMark carve-out approval path & tasks

Team — summarizing next steps so we can align on an approval timeline: 

1) Product (Karthik) defines SLI/SLO language (JIRA: JIRA-INF-4523) and capacity headroom estimate. Deliverable: proposed SLO language and monthly cost delta. Due: Tue EOD.
2) Infra/Ops (Marissa) scopes load test and reserve a dedicated pool for a 48-hour run. Deliverable: test report + runbook for pinning and failover. Due: Wed EOD.
3) Finance (Laura) prepares the credit schedule and commercial language; propose a draft SOW appendix. Deliverable: draft SOW + cost model. Due: Wed EOD.
4) Legal to prepare a limited carve-out clause and MSA/SOW language (we will circulate after product/finance agree).

Estimated implementation lift: 2-3 engineering sprints for automation & monitoring if we need changes to routing policies, plus an ops-runbook update. Preliminary monthly delta estimate: $8k–$15k depending on reserved headroom and standby region.

If all sign-offs occur this week we can provide RiverMark a redline-ready SOW by Thu and route DocuSign by next week. Laura — can you confirm you will own the commercial thread? Karthik/Marissa — ack on the timeline?

Vivek
